key_insight: An AI system can change even when its public name stays the same. The paper argues that meaningful version identifiers are essential for tracking those changes and supporting reliable research and oversight.
problem_solved: Providers update models and system integrations without changing public identifiers, making it difficult to know which system was evaluated, reproduce results, or conduct regulatory oversight.
method: Identify the accountability and reproducibility gaps caused by unchanged identifiers after AI system updates.
Argue for versioning that reflects changes to both models and their system integrations.
Frame meaningful versioning around the needs of researchers and regulators.
impact: Meaningful versioning would help practitioners connect evaluations and deployments to specific AI system versions. It would also strengthen reproducibility and regulatory accountability.
visual_elements: An update timeline showing different AI systems hidden behind one unchanged public name.
A before-and-after diagram contrasting a fixed model label with distinct version identifiers.
A layered diagram separating the model from its system integrations.
Linked icons for version identification, reproducible experiments, and regulatory oversight.
paper_authors: Vasilios Mavroudis, Dan Ristea, Lauritz Morlock, Carlos Mougan
